items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Joe Jones and the Jimmy Garrison was playing bass.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was on this date, yeah. Joe Jones and the Jimmy Garrison was playing bass. And what's -- that's an interesting story, I'll get to that one in a moment. But Phil Woods as I told you had been playing this number, the Midnight Sun and (inaudible). But Benny on this date gave the solo to Coleman Hawkins. And Phil Woods never heard so much that 'Midnight Sun never Sets' in his life, as Coleman Hawkins played. The old man, the gray old man. You know. He played this tune, he played it sideways, up and down,…

But this is interesting how styles, you know, they -- it's just timeless, you know. That -- it proves that if you just stay on top of music, just stay and listen and you can -- your style stays young, you know. Of course now I have been thrown in with some Dixieland groups, some concerts here in San Diego. It's a Dixieland club there, and they always called me, and it's the most unpleasant thing in the world. I imagine -- well, I'll tell you what. It's not Dixieland per se, but it's the exponents of it, it's the…
